text: Working with APIs allows different software applications to communicate with each other. To access data from an API, you typically send HTTP requests, such as GET for retrieving information or POST for sending data. The response is often formatted in JSON, a lightweight data structure that is easy for programs to read. Many APIs require authentication, usually through an API key, to ensure only authorised users can access them. It's also important to be aware of rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a given time period. Finally, good error handling is essential; when an API returns an error code, your code should respond gracefully without crashing.
